Have you ever seen an IP address like this on your home or office computer?
This is what is called a private IP address.
However, you can open Google, watch YouTube, and use the Internet normally from a computer with this IP address.
Doesn't that seem a little strange?
This is because a private IP address is not supposed to be an address for direct communication on the Internet.
Even so, why can you access the Internet?
What are NAT masquerade and SNAT?｜toshi
What are NAT masquerade and SNAT?

NAT (Network Address Translation) is one of the technologies that supports the internet communication we use every day behind the scenes. Among them, masquerade and SNAT are important mechanisms for translating source IP addresses. Although they are similar, they are used in different situations and have different characteristics.
In this article, I will explain masquerade and SNAT in an easy-to-understand way using analogies!

Masquerade is a type of NAT that performs communication by "disguising" the source IP address. It is particularly useful in environments that use dynamic IP addresses. By converting private IPs in an internal network to an external public IP, multiple devices can share a single public IP.
Analogy: Communication while wearing a mask
Communication using masquerade is like a "participant in a masquerade ball."
When all family members (devices with private IPs) send a letter, they send it under the "family representative's name" (the router's public IP) instead of their own names.
